newsitem.title: JAPAN: Markets will eventually reflect recovery - Japan MOF.
newsitem.headline: Markets will eventually reflect recovery - Japan MOF.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday that Japan's economic recovery will likely pick up in the latter of the next fiscal year, and the recovery will eventually be reflected in the financial markets.
He said that the economy may take "one step forward and one step back" in the first half of the next fiscal year starting April 1997.
However, supported by various reforms the economic conditions will likely become steadier in the latter half of the year, he said.
"I think the financial markets will eventually reflect this," he said.
He added that the stock market seemed to be moving on various factors towards the year-end.

The finance minister also said that tax cuts carried out over the past three years have helped to strengthen Japan's economy to a point where it it is likely to be able to withstand the negative effects from a rise in the consumption tax from April.
